To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a new methodology for the simultaneous (13)C isotopic analysis of glycerol, ethanol and wine was developed using liquid chromatography coupled with isotope ratio mass spectroscopy.
we have developed the first method to determine (13)C in wine glycerol using a single LC-IRMS analysis.
a novel procedure was established to determine the (13)C/12C isotope ratio of wine glycerot and ethanol simultaneously by LC-IRMS, and it was validated for the first time.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of new analytical methodologies for the simultaneous determination of (13)C in wine glycerol, ethanol and water by liquid chromatography/isotopic ratio mass spectrometric (LC-IR-MS) analysis.
the development of a new method for the simultaneous (13)C isotope analysis of wine glycol and ethanol, using LC coupled to IRMS.

the development of a new method that will allow the simultaneous (13)C/ (12)C determination in wine of two important metabolites, glycerol and ethyl alcohol, with a high analytical precision and accuracy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the new developed method is suitable and accurate for simultaneous (13)C isotopic analysis of ethanol and glycerol in wine samples.
the LC-IRMS methodology developed in this work is a powerful and reliable tool for the simultaneous isotopic characterization of wine glycosylated compounds (glycerol) and ethanol.
LC-IRMS represents a promising tool for isotopic characterization of wine glycolipids and ethanol.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this is a new method for the simultaneous determination of (13)C in wine glycerol, ethanol and other wine compounds.

the proposed method allows a fast, precise and accurate determination of glycerol (and ethanol) (13)C isotope ratios from a liquid sample, with no previous isolation or purification of glycerol or other sample preparation.
the new LC-IRMS procedure allows simultaneous determination of (13)C in glycerol and (13)C and (2)H in ethanol, and it is the first method that allows (2)H determination in ethanol in wine samples.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is now possible to determine the isotopic ratio of glycerol directly from a liquid matrix without any previous sample treatment.
the LC-IRMS methodology developed is a simple and rapid method to determine the (13)C content of wine glycerols and ethanol in the same run.
the new developed methodology is a powerful tool to determine the (13)C enrichment of both wine ethanol and glycerol, in a single run, and with a very low sample volume.
